Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. ## context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service -- even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer -- your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

## serena
CRITICAL: Before starting to work on a coding task, call the `initial_instructions` tool to read the 'Serena Instructions Manual'.

## tokensave
tokensave is a code-graph MCP server. Start with tokensave_context for any code exploration task — it returns relevant symbols, relationships, and code snippets for a natural-language query. Use tokensave_search to find specific symbols by name. Discovery and analysis tools are read-only and safe to call in parallel. Edit and session-memory tools can mutate local project state and declare readOnlyHint=false. When a tool result contains a `tokensave_metrics:` line, report the savings to the user (e.g. 'TokenSave\'d ~N tokens').

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud (requires claude.ai account access)). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

5	/// Orchestrates a post-transcription diarization pass.
6	///
7	/// Loads stored audio for a recording, runs it through the diarization engine
8	/// to identify speaker boundaries, then merges those boundaries with the
9	/// transcription segments to produce a fully attributed ``DiarizedTranscript``.
10	///
11	/// Each ``TranscriptionSegment`` is assigned the speaker whose time range has
12	/// the maximum overlap with it. Segments that fall entirely outside all speaker
13	/// ranges are labelled `"Unknown"`.
14	///
15	/// All I/O is delegated to injected domain protocols — this actor contains no
16	/// direct file-system, audio-framework, or inference dependencies.
17	public actor DiarizeMeetingUseCase {
18	
19	    // MARK: - Dependencies
20	
21	    private let diarization: any DiarizationEngine
22	    private let sampleLoader: any AudioSampleLoader
23	    private let reader: any RecordingReadRepository
24	    private let writer: any DiarizationWriteRepository
25	
26	    // MARK: - Logging
27	
28	    private let logger = AppLogger.for(category: "Diarization")
29	
30	    // MARK: - Init
31	
32	    public init(
33	        diarization: any DiarizationEngine,
34	        sampleLoader: any AudioSampleLoader,
35	        reader: any RecordingReadRepository,
36	        writer: any DiarizationWriteRepository
37	    ) {
38	        self.diarization = diarization
39	        self.sampleLoader = sampleLoader
40	        self.reader = reader
41	        self.writer = writer
42	    }
43	
44	    // MARK: - Diarize
45	
46	    /// Produces a diarized transcript by aligning speaker segments with
47	    /// transcription segments for a stored recording.
48	    ///
49	    /// - Parameters:
50	    ///   - recordingId: Unique identifier of the stored recording.
51	    ///   - transcription: The transcription result to enrich with speaker labels.
52	    /// - Returns: A ``DiarizedTranscript`` where every segment carries a speaker
53	    ///   identity, or `"Unknown"` when no speaker segment overlaps it.
54	    /// - Throws: Any error produced by storage, sample loader, or diarization —
55	    ///   errors are never swallowed here.
56	    public func diarize(
57	        recordingId: RecordingID,
58	        transcription: TranscriptionResult,
59	    ) async throws -> DiarizedTranscript {
60	        logger.info("Starting diarization for \(recordingId.rawValue, privacy: .public)")
61	
62	        let recording = try await reader.getRecording(id: recordingId)
63	        let audioURL = recording.metadata.audioURL
64	        logger.info("Retrieved recording: \(recording.metadata.id, privacy: .public)")
65	
66	        let samples = try await sampleLoader.loadSamples(from: audioURL)
67	        // swiftlint:disable:next line_length
68	        logger.info("Loaded \(samples.count, privacy: .public) samples from \(audioURL.lastPathComponent, privacy: .public)")
69	
70	        let startTime = CFAbsoluteTimeGetCurrent()
71	        let speakerSegments = try await runDiarization(samples: samples)
72	        let diarizedSegments = alignSegments(speakers: speakerSegments, transcription: transcription)
73	        let elapsed = CFAbsoluteTimeGetCurrent() - startTime
74	
75	        let uniqueSpeakers = Set(speakerSegments.map(\.speakerId))
76	        // swiftlint:disable:next line_length
77	        logger.info("Merged \(diarizedSegments.count, privacy: .public) segments across \(uniqueSpeakers.count, privacy: .public) speakers in \(elapsed, format: .fixed(precision: 3), privacy: .public)s")
78	
79	        let diarizedTranscript = DiarizedTranscript(
80	            segments: diarizedSegments,
81	            speakerCount: uniqueSpeakers.count,
82	            processingTime: elapsed,
83	        )
84	
85	        try await writer.attachDiarization(id: recordingId, diarization: diarizedTranscript)
86	        logger.info("Saved \(diarizedTranscript.segments.count, privacy: .public) segments for \(recordingId, privacy: .private)")
87	
88	        return diarizedTranscript
89	    }
90	
91	    // MARK: - Helpers
92	
93	    /// Prepares the diarization engine if needed and runs it on the given samples.
94	    private func runDiarization(samples: [Float]) async throws -> [SpeakerSegment] {
95	        if await !diarization.isReady() { try await diarization.prepare() }
96	        let segments = try await diarization.diarize(samples: samples, sampleRate: 16000)
97	        logger.info("Diarization engine returned \(segments.count, privacy: .public) speaker segments")
98	        for (i, seg) in segments.prefix(10).enumerated() {
99	            // swiftlint:disable:next line_length
100	            logger.info("  speaker[\(i, privacy: .public)]: id=\(seg.speakerId, privacy: .public) start=\(seg.startTime, format: .fixed(precision: 1), privacy: .public)s end=\(seg.endTime, format: .fixed(precision: 1), privacy: .public)s")
101	        }
102	        return segments
103	    }
104	
105	    /// Aligns transcription segments with speaker segments by maximum time overlap.
106	    private func alignSegments(
107	        speakers: [SpeakerSegment],
108	        transcription: TranscriptionResult,
109	    ) -> [DiarizedSegment] {
110	        // swiftlint:disable:next line_length
111	        logger.info("Merging \(speakers.count, privacy: .public) speaker segments × \(transcription.segments.count, privacy: .public) transcription segments")
112	        for (i, seg) in transcription.segments.prefix(5).enumerated() {
113	            // swiftlint:disable:next line_length
114	            logger.info("  transcript[\(i, privacy: .public)]: start=\(seg.startTime, format: .fixed(precision: 1), privacy: .public)s end=\(seg.endTime, format: .fixed(precision: 1), privacy: .public)s text=\(String(seg.text.prefix(40)), privacy: .private)")
115	        }
116	        return transcription.segments.map { seg in
117	            let best = speakers
118	                .map { (speaker: $0, overlap: overlapDuration($0, seg)) }
119	                .max(by: { $0.overlap < $1.overlap })
120	            let speakerId: SpeakerID = if let b = best, b.overlap > 0 { b.speaker.speakerId } else { .unknown }
121	            return DiarizedSegment(
122	                text: seg.text,
123	                speakerId: speakerId,
124	                startTime: seg.startTime,
125	                endTime: seg.endTime,
126	                confidence: seg.confidence,
127	            )
128	        }
129	    }
130	
131	    nonisolated private func overlapDuration(
132	        _ speaker: SpeakerSegment,
133	        _ transcript: TranscriptionSegment,
134	    ) -> TimeInterval {
135	        max(0, min(speaker.endTime, transcript.endTime) - max(speaker.startTime, transcript.startTime))
136	    }
137	}

# THE RECORD

Local-first macOS meeting transcription app. Swift 6.2, Clean Architecture, TDD.

## Resume

Read `CURRENT_STATE.md` — it has the current epic, phase, and next action.

## Orchestration

This file is the conductor. Epics execute in dependency order:

```
COMPLETED                                    REMAINING
─────────                                    ─────────
Epic 1: Core Recording ─┐
Epic 1.5: Capture Fixes  ├──→ Epic 3.5: Parakeet + Telemetry (no UI)
Epic 3: Transcription    │
Epic 4: Diarization     ─┘──→ Epic 5: Menu Bar UI (needs desk)
Epic 2: Storage         ─┘──→ Epic 6: Summarization (MLX/GPU)
                              Epic 7: Streaming + Translation
                              Epic 8: THE RECORD Engine (MCP + NLP)
```

Each epic follows 5 phases: **REFINE** (SPEC) → **PLAN** (TASKS.md) → **PROPERTIES** (formal properties) → **ACT** (code) → **VALIDATE** (integration).
Human checkpoint after PLAN and before ACT. Within ACT, layers build sequentially: Domain → Business → Infrastructure → Presentation.

PROPERTIES.md (template at `docs/planning/PROPERTIES-TEMPLATE.md`) captures 11 property categories:
FUNCTIONAL, SAFETY, LIVENESS, PERFORMANCE, SECURITY, RELIABILITY, CONCURRENCY, OBSERVABILITY, UX, DATA INTEGRITY, PRIVACY.
Each property drives test generation (RED briefs) and reviewer validation (traceability matrix).

## Skills (Progressive Disclosure)

Read the skill file when entering that phase. Don't load all skills upfront.

| Phase / Layer | Skill File to Read |
|---------------|-------------------|
| Full epic workflow | `.claude/skills/therecord-epic-executor/SKILL.md` |
| Domain types | `.claude/skills/therecord-domain-architect/SKILL.md` |
| Business actors | `.claude/skills/therecord-business-architect/SKILL.md` |
| Infrastructure | `.claude/skills/therecord-infrastructure-architect/SKILL.md` |
| Presentation | `.claude/skills/therecord-presentation-architect/SKILL.md` |
| Quality gate | `.claude/skills/therecord-integration-validator/SKILL.md` |
| Pre-merge bug hunt | `.claude/skills/therecord-bug-hunt/SKILL.md` |

## Architecture (4-Layer Clean)

```
Domain (structs, enums, protocols)  ←  Business (actors)  ←  Infrastructure (actors)
                                    ←  Presentation (@MainActor classes)
```

**Boundaries enforced by hooks:**
- Domain: only `import Foundation`
- Business: Domain + Foundation + OSLog
- Infrastructure: implements Domain protocols, translates all external errors to domain errors
- Presentation: Business + Domain + SwiftUI

**Also enforced by hooks:**
- File size limits: Domain 100, Business 300, Infrastructure 300, ViewModels 200, Views 150
- No `@unchecked Sendable` outside Infrastructure/Audio and Domain/Audio/AudioBuffer
- TDD guard: warns if writing source without corresponding test file

## Integration Test Environment Variables

```bash
# Enable integration tests (real WhisperKit, DuckDB, FluidAudio inference)
RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 python3 scripts/test.py --filter "SomeSuite" --no-parallel

# Enable MLX summarization tests (requires app bundle context for metallib — see #80, #81)
RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 RUN_MLX_TESTS=1 python3 scripts/test.py --filter "SummarizationModelComparison" --no-parallel
```

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS` | unset (skipped) | Enables real-hardware integration suites: WhisperKit, DuckDB, FluidAudio, pipeline |
| `RUN_MLX_TESTS` | unset (skipped) | Enables MLX summarization tests. Requires metallib accessible from bundle (blocked until #81 lands) |

Use `--no-parallel` for integration tests to prevent `swift test --parallel` from buffering stdout during long-running inference.

## TDD Order

1. Write test → 2. Verify it FAILS (RED) → 3. Implement → 4. Verify it PASSES (GREEN) → 5. Commit together

## Rename / Refactor Protocol

# No Embedded Languages ## What This Is A mandatory rule preventing inline embedding of non-Swift languages in Swift source files. All foreign-language content must live in dedicated files so it can be linted, reviewed, and tested as its own source. ## When to Apply Every time you write or edit Swift code that would contain non-Swift content inline — SQL, JSON schemas, LLM prompts, shell commands, HTML, regex, or any other language embedded as string literals. ## The Rule **Never embed non-Swift languages as inline string literals in Swift source.** Extract them into dedicated files and reference them from Swift. ### What counts as an embedded language | Language | Example | Extract to | |----------|---------|-----------| | SQL | `"SELECT ... FROM ..."` | `*SQL.swift` enum with static funcs | | LLM prompts | `"You are a ..."` | `*Prompts.swift` enum with static funcs | | JSON schemas/templates | `{"key": "..."}` | `*Prompts.swift` or `*Schema.swift` | | JSON-RPC / wire protocols | `["jsonrpc": "2.0", ...]` | `*Protocol.swift` enum | | Shell commands | `"/bin/sh -c ..."` | `*Commands.swift` enum | | HTML templates | `"
...
"` | `*Templates.swift` enum | | Regex patterns | `"^[a-z]+\\d{3}$"` | `*Patterns.swift` enum | ### Naming convention The extracted file lives next to the consumer and uses a suffix that describes the embedded language: ``` Infrastructure/Storage/DuckDBSQL.swift — SQL for DuckDBStorageActor Infrastructure/Summarization/SummarizationPrompts.swift — LLM prompts Infrastructure/MCP/MCPProtocol.swift — JSON-RPC wire format ``` ### Pattern Use a caseless `enum` with static functions or properties: ```swift enum DuckDBSQL { static let createRecordings = "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ..." static func selectRecording(id: String) -> String { ... } } ``` The consumer calls `DuckDBSQL.selectRecording(id: id)` — no inline SQL. ## Why 1. **Lintable** — SQL, JSON, and prompts in their own files can have dedicated lint rules, line length checks, and format validation without fighting Swift's string escaping. 2. **Reviewable** — PRs that change SQL or prompts show up as changes to a clearly-named file, not buried inside business logic. 3. **Testable** — extracted prompts and queries can be unit tested for structure, required fields, and format without instantiating the consumer. 4. **Discoverable** — `grep` for all SQL → look in `*SQL.swift`. Grep for all prompts → look in `*Prompts.swift`. No hunting through actor files. 5. **Drift-resistant** — when a DTO struct changes shape, the co-located prompt file is an obvious place to update. Inline strings get forgotten. ## Exceptions - **Trivial single-value strings** that happen to be another language but are under 80 characters and non-reusable (e.g. `"DELETE FROM x WHERE id = ?"`) may stay inline if extracting would add ceremony without value. - **Test fixtures** — test files may contain inline examples for readability. ## Existing extractions | File | Contains | Consumer | |------|----------|----------| | `DuckDBSQL.swift` | All DuckDB SQL | `DuckDBStorageActor` | | `SummarizationPrompts.swift` | LLM prompt + JSON schema | `MLXSummarizationPlugin` | | `MCPProtocol.swift` | JSON-RPC request builder | `GenericMCPProvider` |

# No Embedded Languages ## What This Is A mandatory rule preventing inline embedding of non-Swift languages in Swift source files. All foreign-language content must live in dedicated files so it can be linted, reviewed, and tested as its own source. ## When to Apply Every time you write or edit Swift code that would contain non-Swift content inline — SQL, JSON schemas, LLM prompts, shell commands, HTML, regex, or any other language embedded as string literals. ## The Rule **Never embed non-Swift languages as inline string literals in Swift source.** Extract them into dedicated files and reference them from Swift. ### What counts as an embedded language | Language | Example | Extract to | |----------|---------|-----------| | SQL | `"SELECT ... FROM ..."` | `*SQL.swift` enum with static funcs | | LLM prompts | `"You are a ..."` | `*Prompts.swift` enum with static funcs | | JSON schemas/templates | `{"key": "..."}` | `*Prompts.swift` or `*Schema.swift` | | JSON-RPC / wire protocols | `["jsonrpc": "2.0", ...]` | `*Protocol.swift` enum | | Shell commands | `"/bin/sh -c ..."` | `*Commands.swift` enum | | HTML templates | `"
...
"` | `*Templates.swift` enum | | Regex patterns | `"^[a-z]+\\d{3}$"` | `*Patterns.swift` enum | ### Naming convention The extracted file lives next to the consumer and uses a suffix that describes the embedded language: ``` Infrastructure/Storage/DuckDBSQL.swift — SQL for DuckDBStorageActor Infrastructure/Summarization/SummarizationPrompts.swift — LLM prompts Infrastructure/MCP/MCPProtocol.swift — JSON-RPC wire format ``` ### Pattern Use a caseless `enum` with static functions or properties: ```swift enum DuckDBSQL { static let createRecordings = "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ..." static func selectRecording(id: String) -> String { ... } } ``` The consumer calls `DuckDBSQL.selectRecording(id: id)` — no inline SQL. ## Why 1. **Lintable** — SQL, JSON, and prompts in their own files can have dedicated lint rules, line length checks, and format validation without fighting Swift's string escaping. 2. **Reviewable** — PRs that change SQL or prompts show up as changes to a clearly-named file, not buried inside business logic. 3. **Testable** — extracted prompts and queries can be unit tested for structure, required fields, and format without instantiating the consumer. 4. **Discoverable** — `grep` for all SQL → look in `*SQL.swift`. Grep for all prompts → look in `*Prompts.swift`. No hunting through actor files. 5. **Drift-resistant** — when a DTO struct changes shape, the co-located prompt file is an obvious place to update. Inline strings get forgotten. ## Exceptions - **Trivial single-value strings** that happen to be another language but are under 80 characters and non-reusable (e.g. `"DELETE FROM x WHERE id = ?"`) may stay inline if extracting would add ceremony without value. - **Test fixtures** — test files may contain inline examples for readability. ## Existing extractions | File | Contains | Consumer | |------|----------|----------| | `DuckDBSQL.swift` | All DuckDB SQL | `DuckDBStorageActor` | | `SummarizationPrompts.swift` | LLM prompt + JSON schema | `MLXSummarizationPlugin` | | `MCPProtocol.swift` | JSON-RPC request builder | `GenericMCPProvider` |

5	// MARK: - Error Translation Matrix
6	
7	//
8	// External Error                          → Domain Error
9	// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
10	// url is not a file URL                   → TranscriptionError.inferenceFailed(underlying: URLError(.unsupportedURL))
11	// File does not exist on disk             → TranscriptionError.inferenceFailed(underlying: CocoaError(.fileNoSuchFile))
12	// CocoaError.fileReadNoPermission         → TranscriptionError.inferenceFailed(underlying: error)
13	// CocoaError.fileReadUnknown              → TranscriptionError.inferenceFailed(underlying: error)
14	// File size ≤ 44 bytes (no PCM payload)   → TranscriptionError.audioTooShort
15	// Zero PCM samples after header strip     → TranscriptionError.audioTooShort
16	// Any other Data / I/O error              → TranscriptionError.inferenceFailed(underlying: error)
17	//
18	// MARK: - Thread Safety
19	
20	//
21	// AudioFileLoader is a struct with no mutable state. It is automatically
22	// Sendable (all stored properties are `let` and `Logger` is Sendable).
23	// `loadSamples` is declared `async throws` to satisfy the `AudioSampleLoader`
24	// protocol; callers `await` the async work, not an actor hop.
25	
26	/// Infrastructure implementation of ``AudioSampleLoader`` that reads a
27	/// standard WAV file from disk.
28	///
29	/// Strips the canonical 44-byte RIFF/WAV header, interprets the body as
30	/// little-endian 16-bit signed PCM samples, and normalises them to 32-bit
31	/// float in the range `[-1.0, 1.0]` by dividing by 32 768.0.
32	///
33	/// > Important: Only plain PCM WAV files with a 44-byte header are
34	/// > supported. Compressed, multi-chunk, or non-PCM WAV variants are not
35	/// > decoded.
36	public struct AudioFileLoader: AudioSampleLoader {
37	    // MARK: - Constants
38	
39	    /// Number of bytes in a standard RIFF/WAV header.
40	    private static let wavHeaderSize = 44
41	
42	    /// Divisor used to normalise `Int16` samples to `[-1.0, 1.0]`.
43	    private static let normalisationDivisor: Float = 32768.0
44	
45	    // MARK: - Private State
46	
47	    private let logger = AppLogger.for(category: "AudioLoader")
48	
49	    // MARK: - Init
50	
51	    public init() {}
52	
53	    // MARK: - AudioSampleLoader
54	
55	    /// Loads PCM audio samples from a WAV file URL.
56	    ///
57	    /// - Parameter url: A `file://` URL pointing to a WAV file with a
58	    ///   44-byte RIFF header followed by little-endian Int16 PCM data.
59	    /// - Returns: Normalised mono Float32 samples in `[-1.0, 1.0]`.
60	    /// - Throws: ``TranscriptionError/audioTooShort`` when the file has no
61	    ///   usable PCM payload; ``TranscriptionError/inferenceFailed(underlying:)``
62	    ///   for all other I/O failures.
63	    public func loadSamples(from url: URL) async throws -> [Float] {
64	        logger.debug("loadSamples requested: \(url.lastPathComponent, privacy: .private)")
65	
66	        // DPS-1: Validate URL type at boundary.
67	        guard url.isFileURL else {
68	            logger.error("Rejected non-file URL: \(url.absoluteString, privacy: .public)")
69	            throw TranscriptionError.inferenceFailed(underlying: URLError(.unsupportedURL))
70	        }
71	
72	        // Validate file existence before attempting a read.
73	        guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: url.path) else {
74	            logger.error("File not found: \(url.path, privacy: .private)")
75	            throw TranscriptionError.inferenceFailed(
76	                underlying: CocoaError(.fileNoSuchFile)
77	            )
78	        }
79	
80	        // Read raw bytes — translate all I/O errors to domain errors.
81	        let data: Data
82	        do {
83	            data = try await Task.detached(priority: .utility) {
84	                try Data(contentsOf: url, options: .mappedIfSafe)
85	            }.value
86	        } catch {
87	            let errDesc = String(reflecting: error)
88	            logger.error("Read failed (\(errDesc, privacy: .private))")
89	            throw TranscriptionError.inferenceFailed(underlying: error)
90	        }
91	
92	        logger.debug("Read \(data.count, privacy: .public) bytes from \(url.lastPathComponent, privacy: .private)")
93	
94	        // Validate minimum file size: header + at least one Int16 sample.
95	        guard data.count > Self.wavHeaderSize else {
96	            logger.error(
97	                "File too short: \(data.count, privacy: .public) bytes, need >\(Self.wavHeaderSize, privacy: .public)"
98	            )
99	            throw TranscriptionError.audioTooShort
100	        }
101	
102	        // Strip the 44-byte WAV header; remainder is raw PCM payload.
103	        let pcmData = data.dropFirst(Self.wavHeaderSize)
104	
105	        // Integer division: any trailing partial byte is silently ignored.
106	        let sampleCount = pcmData.count / MemoryLayout<Int16>.size
107	
108	        guard sampleCount > 0 else {
109	            logger.error("No complete Int16 samples in PCM payload")
110	            throw TranscriptionError.audioTooShort
111	        }
112	
113	        logger.debug("Converting \(sampleCount, privacy: .private) Int16 samples to Float32")
114	
115	        // Convert little-endian Int16 PCM → normalised Float32.
116	        // Byte-level access avoids alignment concerns from Data slice offsets.
117	        let samples = Self.convertInt16ToFloat(pcmData: pcmData, sampleCount: sampleCount)
118	
119	        logger.info(
120	            "Loaded \(samples.count, privacy: .public) samples from \(url.lastPathComponent, privacy: .public)"
121	        )
122	        return samples
123	    }
124	
125	    // MARK: - Private Helpers
126	
127	    /// Converts a little-endian Int16 PCM byte sequence to normalised Float32.
128	    ///
129	    /// - Parameters:
130	    ///   - pcmData: Raw PCM bytes (header already stripped).
131	    ///   - sampleCount: Number of complete 2-byte samples available.
132	    /// - Returns: Array of Float32 values in `[-1.0, 1.0]`.
133	    private static func convertInt16ToFloat(
134	        pcmData: Data,
135	        sampleCount: Int
136	    ) -> [Float] {
137	        var samples = [Float]()
138	        samples.reserveCapacity(sampleCount)
139	
140	        let base = pcmData.startIndex
141	        for i in 0 ..< sampleCount {
142	            let byteOffset = i * MemoryLayout<Int16>.size
143	            let lo = pcmData[base + byteOffset]
144	            let hi = pcmData[base + byteOffset + 1]
145	            // Reconstruct little-endian signed 16-bit value.
146	            let raw = Int16(bitPattern: UInt16(lo) | (UInt16(hi) << 8))
147	            samples.append(Float(raw) / normalisationDivisor)
148	        }
149	
150	        return samples
151	    }
152	}

1	import Foundation
2	import Logging

5	/// Use case that initiates a new audio recording session.
6	///
7	/// Validates that no recording is already in progress, delegates capture to the
8	/// injected ``AudioCaptureEngine``, creates a ``RecordingSession`` value, and
9	/// returns it to the caller. The session is also retained internally so other
10	/// actors can query the active session via ``getCurrentSession()``.
11	///
12	/// ## Concurrency safety
13	///
14	/// A use-case-level state machine (`State`) reserves the recording slot
15	/// **synchronously** — before any `await` — eliminating the check-then-act race
16	/// that existed when the guard relied on `await audioCapture.isRecording()`.
17	/// Two concurrent `start()` calls cannot both proceed past the `.idle` guard
18	/// because the actor serialises synchronous access: the first call transitions
19	/// to `.starting` before it suspends, so the second call sees a non-idle state
20	/// and throws immediately.
21	///
22	/// ## Usage
23	/// ```swift
24	/// let useCase = StartRecordingUseCase(
25	///     audioCapture: captureEngine,
26	///     storage: storageEngine
27	/// )
28	/// let session = try await useCase.start()
29	/// // … later, when the recording is stopped …
30	/// await useCase.sessionDidEnd()
31	/// ```
32	public actor StartRecordingUseCase {
33	
34	    // MARK: - State machine
35	
36	    private enum State {
37	        /// No recording in progress; ready to accept a new session.
38	        case idle
39	        /// `start()` has reserved the slot and is awaiting the capture engine.
40	        case starting
41	        /// Capture is running and a session is live.
42	        case recording
43	    }
44	
45	    // MARK: - Dependencies
46	
47	    private let audioCapture: any AudioCaptureEngine
48	    private let storage: any RecordingWriteRepository
49	    private let micCapture: (any MicCaptureEngine)?
50	    private let queryContext: QueryContextUseCase?
51	
52	    // MARK: - State
53	
54	    private var state: State = .idle
55	    private var currentSession: RecordingSession?
56	    private var activeBufferStream: AudioBufferStream?
57	    private var activeMicStream: AsyncThrowingStream<TaggedAudioBuffer, Error>?
58	
59	    // MARK: - Logging
60	
61	    private let logger = AppLogger.for(category: "StartRecording")
62	
63	    // MARK: - Initialiser
64	
65	    /// Creates a ``StartRecordingUseCase`` with its required dependencies.
66	    ///
67	    /// - Parameters:
68	    ///   - audioCapture: The audio capture backend to start and query.
69	    ///   - storage: The persistence backend for recorded audio files.
70	    ///   - micCapture: Optional microphone capture engine. When provided, the use case
71	    ///     starts both system and microphone capture. When `nil` or when mic start fails,
72	    ///     only system audio is captured and ``getMicStream()`` returns `nil`.
73	    public init(
74	        audioCapture: any AudioCaptureEngine,
75	        storage: any RecordingWriteRepository,
76	        micCapture: (any MicCaptureEngine)? = nil,
77	        queryContext: QueryContextUseCase? = nil,
78	    ) {
79	        self.audioCapture = audioCapture
80	        self.storage = storage
81	        self.micCapture = micCapture
82	        self.queryContext = queryContext
83	    }
84	
85	    // MARK: - Start
86	
87	    /// Starts a new recording session.
88	    ///
89	    /// 1. Atomically reserves the recording slot (`.idle → .starting`) before
90	    ///    any `await`, preventing concurrent callers from both proceeding.
91	    /// 2. Starts the capture engine with a default ``AudioConfiguration``.
92	    /// 3. Constructs and stores a ``RecordingSession`` (`.starting → .recording`).
93	    /// 4. Returns the session to the caller.
94	    ///
95	    /// On any failure the state is rolled back to `.idle` so a subsequent call
96	    /// can succeed.
97	    ///
98	    /// - Returns: A ``RecordingSession`` representing the newly started session.
99	    /// - Throws: ``RecordingError/alreadyRecording`` if a session is already
100	    ///   active (state is `.starting` or `.recording`), or any error propagated
101	    ///   from the audio capture engine.
102	    // sequential setup — extraction would harm readability
103	    // swiftlint:disable:next function_body_length
104	    public func start() async throws -> RecordingSession {
105	        // ── Atomic reservation (no await yet) ────────────────────────────────
106	        // Actor isolation guarantees this guard + assignment is never interleaved
107	        // with another start() call.  The first caller wins; subsequent callers
108	        // see a non-idle state and throw before touching any async code.
109	        guard state == .idle else {
110	            logger
111	                .warning("Start requested while state=\(String(describing: self.state), privacy: .public) — rejecting")
112	            throw RecordingError.alreadyRecording
113	        }
114	        state = .starting // ← reservation committed before the first await
115	
116	        // ── Async work (actor may suspend here) ──────────────────────────────
117	        // Generate the session ID once and pass it through all call sites.
118	        // This ensures INV-001: AudioFile.id == RecordingSession.id
119	        let sessionID = RecordingID.generate()
120	
121	        // Capture T0 before starting either actor so both streams share the same epoch.
122	        let sessionStartTick = mach_absolute_time()
123	        var config = AudioConfiguration()
124	        config.sessionStartTick = sessionStartTick
125	        do {
126	            try Task.checkCancellation()
127	            let bufferStream = try await audioCapture.start(sessionID: sessionID, configuration: config)
128	            activeBufferStream = bufferStream
129	            logger.info("Audio capture started — stream id: \(bufferStream.id, privacy: .public)")
130	
131	            // ── Optional mic capture ───────────────────────────────────────────
132	            if let mic = micCapture {
133	                // Mic failure is no longer swallowed (Epic #343). We propagate the
134	                // error so the UI can alert the user rather than silently recording
135	                // system-audio only when they expected both tracks.
136	                let micStream = try await mic.start(sessionStartTick: sessionStartTick)
137	                activeMicStream = micStream
138	                logger.info("Mic capture started — dual-track stream active")
139	            }
140	
141	            let session = RecordingSession(
142	                id: sessionID,
143	                startedAt: Date(),
144	                configuration: config,
145	            )
146	
147	            // Persist stub immediately so a crash mid-recording leaves a recoverable row (#161).
148	            try await storage.markSessionStarted(id: session.id, startedAt: session.startedAt)
149	            state = .recording
150	            currentSession = session
151	            await queryContext?.setRecording(true)
152	            logger.info("Recording session started: \(session.id, privacy: .public)")
153	            return session
154	        } catch {
155	            // Roll back so the next start() attempt can proceed.
156	            state = .idle
157	            // If audio capture was already started before the failure/cancellation,
158	            // stop it to release the HAL tap and WAVWriter (Concern #4).
159	            if activeBufferStream != nil {
160	                do { try await audioCapture.stop() } catch {
161	                    logger
162	                        .warning(
163	                            "Audio capture stop failed during rollback: \(String(reflecting: error), privacy: .private)",
164	                        )
165	                }
166	                activeBufferStream = nil
167	            }
168	            if let mic = micCapture, activeMicStream != nil {
169	                do { try await mic.stop() } catch {
170	                    logger
171	                        .warning(
172	                            "Mic capture stop failed during rollback: \(String(reflecting: error), privacy: .private)",
173	                        )
174	                }
175	                activeMicStream = nil
176	            }
177	            logger
178	                .error("Failed to start capture — state reset to idle: \(String(reflecting: error), privacy: .public)")
179	            throw error
180	        }
181	    }
182	
183	    // MARK: - Session End
184	
185	    /// Marks the current recording as ended and resets state to `.idle`.
186	    ///
187	    /// Call this from the stop use case (or coordinator) after the audio capture
188	    /// has been stopped and the session data has been persisted.  Failing to call
189	    /// this leaves the state machine in `.recording`, blocking any future
190	    /// `start()` call.
191	    ///
192	    /// If a microphone capture engine was provided, its `stop()` is called here.
193	    /// Any error from mic stop is swallowed — the session end is unconditional.
194	    public func sessionDidEnd() async {
195	        logger
196	            .info(
197	                "Recording session ended — resetting to idle (was \(String(describing: self.state), privacy: .public))",
198	            )
199	        do {
200	            try await micCapture?.stop()
201	        } catch {
202	            logger.warning(
203	                "Mic stop failed during sessionDidEnd (swallowed): \(String(reflecting: error), privacy: .private)",
204	            )
205	        }
206	        state = .idle
207	        currentSession = nil
208	        activeBufferStream = nil
209	        activeMicStream = nil
210	        await queryContext?.setRecording(false)
211	    }
212	
213	    /// Returns the system audio stream when capture is active, or `nil` otherwise.
214	    public func getSystemStream() -> AudioBufferStream? {
215	        activeBufferStream
216	    }
217	
218	    /// Returns the raw microphone stream when dual-track capture is active.
219	    ///
220	    /// Returns `nil` when no `micCapture` was provided, or when mic `start()` failed.
221	    public func getMicStream() -> AsyncThrowingStream<TaggedAudioBuffer, Error>? {
222	        activeMicStream
223	    }
224	
225	    // MARK: - Session Query
226	
227	    /// Returns the current recording session, or `nil` when no session is active.
228	    public func getCurrentSession() -> RecordingSession? {
229	        currentSession
230	    }
231	
232	    /// Returns the active session's ID, or `nil` when no recording is in progress.
233	    public func activeSessionId() -> RecordingID? {
234	        currentSession?.id
235	    }

15	/// Owns the live Core Audio tap and aggregate device IDs so they are destroyed
16	/// deterministically in `deinit` — even if `stop()` is never called on the actor.
17	///
18	/// Mirrors the `SpeexResources` pattern in `AECProcessorActor`.

20	    var tapID: AudioObjectID = .init(kAudioObjectUnknown)
21	    var aggregateDeviceID: AudioObjectID = .init(kAudioObjectUnknown)
22	
23	    deinit {
24	        if aggregateDeviceID != kAudioObjectUnknown {
25	            AudioHardwareDestroyAggregateDevice(aggregateDeviceID)

35	public actor CoreAudioTapCaptureActor: AudioCaptureEngine, SelfRecordingStateProvider {
36	    private let audioQueue = DispatchSerialQueue(label: "app.the-record.coreaudio", qos: .userInitiated)

45	    // all access goes through the actor's serial executor regardless of Swift access level.
46	    // TODO(5.8): Resolve via module-level access control when Infrastructure becomes its own SwiftPM target.
47	    var state: AudioCaptureState = .idle
48	    /// Core Audio tap and aggregate device IDs. Destroyed in `CoreAudioResources.deinit`
49	    /// as a safety net if `stop()` is never called.
50	    let resources = CoreAudioResources()
51	    var engine: AVAudioEngine?
52	    var wavWriter: WAVWriter?
53	    var sessionID: RecordingID?

80	    public func start(sessionID: RecordingID, configuration: AudioConfiguration) async throws -> AudioBufferStream {
81	        guard state == .idle else { throw AudioError.captureFailed(underlying: nil) }
82	
83	        // Permission probe — before state change or resource allocation (finding #21).
84	        // defaultOutputDeviceUID() failure means audio is non-functional; stay .idle.
85	        let outputUID = try outputDeviceUID ?? Self.defaultOutputDeviceUID()

88	        state = .starting

173	    /// Determines whether a global tap is needed, logging the reason.
174	    private func resolveGlobalTap(matchedBundleIDs: [String]) -> Bool {
175	        if tapAllAudio {
176	            logger.info("Creating global tap (tapAllAudio=true)")
177	            return true
178	        } else if matchedBundleIDs.isEmpty {
179	            logger.info("No matching meeting apps — creating global tap")
180	            return true
181	        } else {
182	            let bundleIDList = matchedBundleIDs.joined(separator: ",")
183	            logger.info("Targeting bundleIDs: \(bundleIDList, privacy: .public)")
184	            return false
185	        }
186	    }

188	    /// Constructs a configured `CATapDescription` for the given tap strategy.
189	    private nonisolated func buildTapDescription(
190	        isGlobalTap: Bool,
191	        matchedBundleIDs: [String],
192	        configuration: AudioConfiguration,
193	        tapUUID: UUID,
194	        outputUID: String
195	    ) -> CATapDescription {
196	        let tapDesc: CATapDescription
197	        if isGlobalTap {
198	            if configuration.channels == 1 {
199	                tapDesc = CATapDescription(monoGlobalTapButExcludeProcesses: [])
200	            } else {
201	                tapDesc = CATapDescription(stereoGlobalTapButExcludeProcesses: [])
202	            }
203	        } else if #available(macOS 26, *) {
204	            tapDesc = CATapDescription()
205	            tapDesc.bundleIDs = matchedBundleIDs
206	        } else {
207	            // macOS 15: bundleIDs targeting requires macOS 26 — fall back to global tap
208	            if configuration.channels == 1 {
209	                tapDesc = CATapDescription(monoGlobalTapButExcludeProcesses: [])
210	            } else {
211	                tapDesc = CATapDescription(stereoGlobalTapButExcludeProcesses: [])
212	            }
213	        }
214	
215	        tapDesc.name = "THE RECORD System Audio"
216	        tapDesc.uuid = tapUUID
217	        tapDesc.isPrivate = true
218	        tapDesc.muteBehavior = .unmuted
219	        tapDesc.isMixdown = true
220	        tapDesc.isMono = configuration.channels == 1
221	        tapDesc.isExclusive = false
222	        tapDesc.deviceUID = outputUID
223	        tapDesc.stream = 0
224	        if #available(macOS 26, *) { tapDesc.isProcessRestoreEnabled = true }
225	
226	        return tapDesc
227	    }

229	    public func stop() async throws -> AudioFile {
230	        guard state == .recording else {
231	            throw AudioError.captureFailed(underlying: nil)
232	        }
233	        state = .stopping
234	        // T014: guarantee state returns to .idle even if finalize() throws or
235	        // sessionFileURL is nil. Without this defer, any early throw left the
236	        // actor permanently at .stopping, blocking subsequent start() calls.
237	        defer { if state == .stopping { cleanup()
238	            state = .idle
239	        } }
240	
241	        streamContinuation?.finish()
242	
243	        // Teardown order: remove tap → clear device → stop engine → destroy aggregate → destroy tap
244	        if let engine {
245	            engine.inputNode.removeTap(onBus: 0)
246	
247	            if let audioUnit = engine.inputNode.audioUnit {
248	                var unknownDevID: AudioObjectID = .init(kAudioObjectUnknown)
249	                AudioUnitSetProperty(
250	                    audioUnit,
251	                    kAudioOutputUnitProperty_CurrentDevice,
252	                    kAudioUnitScope_Global, 0,
253	                    &unknownDevID,
254	                    UInt32(MemoryLayout<AudioObjectID>.size)
255	                )
256	            }
257	
258	            engine.stop()
259	            self.engine = nil
260	        }
261	
262	        try await wavWriter?.finalize()
263	
264	        guard let fileURL = sessionFileURL else {
265	            throw AudioError.captureFailed(underlying: nil)
266	        }
267	        let startDate = sessionStartDate ?? Date()
268	        let config = sessionConfiguration ?? AudioConfiguration()
269	        let duration = Date().timeIntervalSince(startDate)
270	        let fileSize = (try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: fileURL.path)[.size] as? Int64) ?? 0
271	        let sampleCount = Int(duration * config.sampleRate)
272	
273	        cleanup()
274	        state = .idle
275	
276	        let durationStr = String(format: "%.1f", duration)
277	        logger.info("Core Audio Tap stopped — duration=\(durationStr, privacy: .private)s")
278	
279	        // Use the session ID that was passed to start() — INV-001: AudioFile.id == RecordingSession.id.
280	        // The fallback should never fire; if it does, the AudioFile.id will not match the
281	        // RecordingSession.id and any downstream join by ID will silently fail.
282	        if sessionID == nil {
283	            logger.error("stop() called with nil sessionID — INV-001 violated: AudioFile.id will not match RecordingSession.id")
284	        }
285	        let fileID = sessionID ?? RecordingID.generate()
286	        return AudioFile(
287	            id: fileID,
288	            url: fileURL,
289	            recordedAt: startDate,
290	            duration: duration,
291	            fileSize: fileSize,
292	            configuration: config,
293	            sampleCount: sampleCount
294	        )
295	    }

298	        state == .recording
299	    }

302	        state == .recording
303	    }

The timing also hints at this: stereo at 16 kHz for 31.19 seconds would be roughly 998,000 samples, close to what was written, with the discrepancy possibly explained by the system audio starting a couple seconds late during setup. 11	extension CoreAudioTapCaptureActor {
12	    nonisolated static func extractFloats(
13	        from bufferList: UnsafePointer<AudioBufferList>,
14	        channelCount: Int
15	    ) -> [Float] {
16	        guard channelCount > 0 else { return [] }
17	
18	        let numberBuffers = Int(bufferList.pointee.mNumberBuffers)
19	        guard numberBuffers > 0 else { return [] }
20	
21	        let firstBuffer = bufferList.pointee.mBuffers
22	
23	        // Single interleaved buffer — return as-is
24	        if numberBuffers == 1, Int(firstBuffer.mNumberChannels) == channelCount {
25	            let count = Int(firstBuffer.mDataByteSize / UInt32(MemoryLayout<Float>.size))
26	            guard let data = firstBuffer.mData?.assumingMemoryBound(to: Float.self) else { return [] }
27	            return Array(UnsafeBufferPointer(start: data, count: count))
28	        }
29	
30	        // Non-interleaved: interleave channels
31	        let rawPtr = UnsafeMutableRawPointer(mutating: bufferList)
32	        let buffersOffset = MemoryLayout<AudioBufferList>.size - MemoryLayout<CoreAudio.AudioBuffer>.stride
33	        let buffersBase = rawPtr.advanced(by: buffersOffset)
34	            .assumingMemoryBound(to: CoreAudio.AudioBuffer.self)
35	
36	        let frameCount = Int(firstBuffer.mDataByteSize) / MemoryLayout<Float>.size
37	        var result: [Float] = []
38	        result.reserveCapacity(frameCount * channelCount)
39	
40	        for frame in 0 ..< frameCount {
41	            for ch in 0 ..< channelCount {
42	                let bufferPtr = buffersBase.advanced(by: ch)
43	                guard let data = bufferPtr.pointee.mData else { continue }
44	                result.append(data.assumingMemoryBound(to: Float.self)[frame])
45	            }
46	        }
47	
48	        return result

import wave, sys, numpy as np
for path in sys.argv[1:]:
    w = wave.open(path, 'rb')
    data = np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()), dtype=np.int16).astype(np.float64)
    rate = w.getframerate()
    # Welch-ish: average magnitude spectrum over 8192-sample windows
    win = 8192
    nwin = len(data) // win
    acc = np.zeros(win // 2 + 1)
    for i in range(nwin):
        seg = data[i*win:(i+1)*win] * np.hanning(win)
        acc += np.abs(np.fft.rfft(seg))
    acc /= max(nwin, 1)
    freqs = np.fft.rfftfreq(win, 1/rate)
    acc_db = 20*np.log10(acc + 1e-9)
    peak = acc_db.max()
    # find rolloff: highest freq where level within 40dB of peak
    above = np.where(acc_db > peak - 40)[0]
    rolloff = freqs[above[-1]] if len(above) else 0
    # print band energies
    bands = [(0,1000),(1000,2000),(2000,3000),(3000,4000),(4000,5000),(5000,6000),(6000,7000),(7000,8000)]
    be = []
    for lo,hi in bands:
        m = (freqs>=lo)&(freqs<hi)
        be.append(round(float(acc_db[m].mean()),1))
    print(f"{path.split('/')[-1]}: rolloff(-40dB)={rolloff:.0f}Hz  band_avg_dB={be}")
EOF

ac /= (ac[0] + 1e-9)
lags = np.arange(n) / 100.0
mask = (lags > 0.5) & (lags < 30)
top = np.argsort(ac[mask])[::-1][:8]
sel = np.where(mask)[0][top]
print("top envelope self-similarity: ", [(f"{lags[i]:.2f}s", round(float(ac[i]),3)) for i in sel])

probe = data[int(probe_t*rate):int((probe_t+1)*rate)]
probe_n = probe - probe.mean()
pn = np.linalg.norm(probe_n)
best = []
step = rate // 50
for off in range(0, len(data)-rate, step):
    seg = data[off:off+rate]
    s = seg - seg.mean()
    d = np.linalg.norm(s)*pn
    if d > 0:
        c = float(probe_n @ s / d)
        best.append((c, off/rate))

import Foundation

public enum GRDBSQL {
    // MARK: - Recordings

    static let insertRecording = """
        INSERT INTO recordings (id, recorded_at, duration, file_size, audio_url, \
        model_id, processing_time, compute_unit, word_count, speaker_count, \
        diarization_time, transcript_text) \
        VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?) \
        ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING
        """

    static let insertPendingSession = """
        INSERT INTO recordings (id, recorded_at, duration, file_size, audio_url, \
        model_id, processing_time, compute_unit, word_count, speaker_count, \
        diarization_time, transcript_text, is_pending) \
        VALUES (?, ?, 0.0, 0, '', '', 0.0, 'none', 0, 0, 0.0, NULL, 1) \
        ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING
        """

    static let upsertRecording = """
        INSERT INTO recordings (id, recorded_at, duration, file_size, audio_url, \
        model_id, processing_time, compute_unit, word_count, speaker_count, \
        diarization_time, transcript_text) \
        VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?) \
        ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET \
        duration = excluded.duration, file_size = excluded.file_size, \
        audio_url = excluded.audio_url, model_id = excluded.model_id, \
        processing_time = excluded.processing_time, compute_unit = excluded.compute_unit, \
        word_count = excluded.word_count, speaker_count = excluded.speaker_count, \
        diarization_time = excluded.diarization_time, \
        transcript_text = excluded.transcript_text, is_pending = 0
        """

    static let selectRecording = """
        SELECT id, recorded_at, duration, file_size, audio_url, \
        model_id, processing_time, compute_unit, word_count, speaker_count, \
        diarization_time, transcript_text, cleaned_mic_audio_url \
        FROM recordings WHERE id = ? AND is_pending = 0
        """

    static let listRecordings = """
        SELECT id, recorded_at, duration, word_count \
        FROM recordings WHERE is_pending = 0 ORDER BY recorded_at DESC
        """

    static let listAllRecordingsWithMetadata = """
        SELECT id, recorded_at, duration, file_size, audio_url, \
        model_id, processing_time, compute_unit, word_count, speaker_count, \
        diarization_time, transcript_text, cleaned_mic_audio_url \
        FROM recordings WHERE is_pending = 0 ORDER BY recorded_at DESC
        """

    static let selectAudioURL = "SELECT audio_url FROM recordings WHERE id = ?"

    static let existsRecording = "SELECT id FROM recordings WHERE id = ?"

    static let deleteRecording = "DELETE FROM recordings WHERE id = ?"

    static let updateTranscript = """
        UPDATE recordings SET transcript_text = ?, \
        model_id = ?, processing_time = ?, \
        compute_unit = ?, word_count = ?, \
        is_pending = 0 \
        WHERE id = ?
        """

    static let updateDiarization = """
        UPDATE recordings SET speaker_count = ?, diarization_time = ? WHERE id = ?
        """

    static let totalStorageSize = "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(file_size), 0) FROM recordings WHERE is_pending = 0"

    static let selectPendingSessions = "SELECT id FROM recordings WHERE is_pending = 1 ORDER BY recorded_at ASC"

    static let updateCleanedMicPath = "UPDATE recordings SET cleaned_mic_audio_url = ? WHERE id = ?"

    static let markNeedsRetranscription = "UPDATE recordings SET needs_retranscription = 1 WHERE id = ?"

    static let selectNeedsRetranscription = """
        SELECT id FROM recordings WHERE needs_retranscription = 1 ORDER BY recorded_at ASC
        """

    static let updateAudioDuration = "UPDATE recordings SET duration = ?, file_size = ? WHERE id = ?"

    static let saveDraftTranscript = "UPDATE recordings SET transcript_draft = ? WHERE id = ? AND transcript_draft IS NULL"

    static let selectTranscriptDraft = "SELECT transcript_draft FROM recordings WHERE id = ?"

    // MARK: - Search

    static let searchTranscripts = """
        SELECT id, recorded_at, duration, word_count \
        FROM recordings WHERE is_pending = 0 AND transcript_text LIKE ? ESCAPE '\\' \
        ORDER BY recorded_at DESC
        """

    // MARK: - Diarized Segments

    static let upsertSegment = """
        INSERT INTO diarized_segments (recording_id, segment_index, text, speaker_id, \
        start_time, end_time, confidence) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?) \
        ON CONFLICT (recording_id, segment_index) DO UPDATE SET \
        text = excluded.text, speaker_id = excluded.speaker_id, \
        start_time = excluded.start_time, end_time = excluded.end_time, \
        confidence = excluded.confidence
        """

    static let deleteSegments = "DELETE FROM diarized_segments WHERE recording_id = ?"

    static let deleteStaleSegments = "DELETE FROM diarized_segments WHERE recording_id = ? AND segment_index >= ?"

    static let selectSegments = """
        SELECT text, speaker_id, start_time, end_time, confidence, word_timings \
        FROM diarized_segments WHERE recording_id = ? ORDER BY segment_index ASC
        """

    static let saveWordTimings = """
        UPDATE diarized_segments SET word_timings = ? WHERE recording_id = ? AND segment_index = ?
        """

    static let getWordTimings = """
        SELECT segment_index, word_timings FROM diarized_segments \
        WHERE recording_id = ? ORDER BY segment_index ASC
        """

    // MARK: - Summaries

    static let upsertSummary = """
        INSERT INTO summaries (recording_id, summary_json, generated_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?) \
        ON CONFLICT (recording_id) DO UPDATE SET \
        summary_json = excluded.summary_json, generated_at = excluded.generated_at
        """

    static let selectSummary = "SELECT summary_json FROM summaries WHERE recording_id = ?"

    static let selectSummaryRecordingIDs = "SELECT recording_id FROM summaries"

    // MARK: - Meeting Notes

    static let upsertNotes = """
        INSERT INTO meeting_notes (meeting_id, notes_text) VALUES (?, ?) \
        ON CONFLICT (meeting_id) DO UPDATE SET notes_text = excluded.notes_text
        """

    static let selectNotes = "SELECT notes_text FROM meeting_notes WHERE meeting_id = ?"

    // MARK: - Commitments

    static let insertCommitment = """
        INSERT INTO commitments (id, description, assignee, due_date, status, meeting_id, created_at) \
        VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?) \
        ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET \
        description = excluded.description, assignee = excluded.assignee, \
        due_date = excluded.due_date, status = excluded.status
        """

    static let selectOpenCommitments = """
        SELECT id, description, assignee, due_date, status, meeting_id, created_at \
        FROM commitments WHERE status = 'open' ORDER BY created_at DESC
        """

    static let selectCommitmentsForMeeting = """
        SELECT id, description, assignee, due_date, status, meeting_id, created_at \
        FROM commitments WHERE meeting_id = ?
        """

    // MARK: - Inference Telemetry

    static let insertTelemetry = """
        INSERT OR IGNORE INTO inference_telemetry \
        (id, recorded_at, model_id, audio_seconds, inference_s, rtf, \
        confidence, sample_count, compute_unit, \
        cpu_pct, mem_mb, gpu_mb, page_faults, \
        os_version, cpu_brand, physical_mem_mb, thermal_state, \
        is_plugged_in, battery_pct) \
        VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)
        """

    // MARK: - Context Cache

    static let selectCached = """
        SELECT title, body, source_url, provider_id, relevance_score \
        FROM context_cache \
        WHERE query_text = ? AND provider_id = ? \
        AND (julianday('now') - julianday(cached_at)) * 86400 < ? \
        ORDER BY relevance_score DESC
        """

    static let deleteCached = "DELETE FROM context_cache WHERE query_text = ? AND provider_id = ?"

    static let insertCached = """
        INSERT INTO context_cache \
        (query_text, title, body, source_url, provider_id, relevance_score, cached_at, embedding) \
        VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, datetime('now'), ?)
        """

    static let selectDistinctQueriesWithEmbeddings = """
        SELECT DISTINCT query_text, embedding FROM context_cache \
        WHERE provider_id = ? AND embedding IS NOT NULL
        """

    static let countCacheEntries = "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM context_cache"

    static let pruneCacheOldest = """
        DELETE FROM context_cache WHERE rowid IN \
        (SELECT rowid FROM context_cache ORDER BY cached_at ASC LIMIT ?)
        """
}

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- codex:codex-rescue: Proactively use when Claude Code is stuck, wants a second implementation or diagnosis pass, needs a deeper root-cause investigation, or should hand a substantial coding task to Codex through the shared runtime (Tools: Bash)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- hookify:conversation-analyzer: Use this agent when analyzing conversation transcripts to find behaviors worth preventing with hooks. Typical triggers include the /hookify command being invoked without arguments, or the user explicitly asking to look back at the current conversation and surface mistakes that should be prevented in the future. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: Read, Grep)
- performance-monitor: Monitor agent execution, track token usage, measure response quality, and optimize workflows (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep)

I'm noticing there are a few related issues that haven't been tracked yet—the tap sample-rate corruption, the silent mic-cleaned WAV files, and the wordTimings drop in attachDiarization. Since the user asked me to review the GitHub issues and I'm seeing gaps in coverage, I should create new issues to document these problems. I'll start with one for the system tap capture not handling device sample-rate and config changes properly.

The stretched WAV timeline from sample-rate mismatches is actually the root cause of diarization and transcript corruption, which ties back to #49 and #194—this is high severity. Then there's the mic-cleaned WAV being digitally silent in production, which relates to the AEC output and connects to #190 and #192. For the wordTimings issue, the upsert doesn't clear old timings when a segment changes, so stale word_timings can persist after re-diarization—that's a real defect worth tracking.

I need to follow the issue creation format with the `[see-something]` prefix and apply the right labels. The ThemeEditorView size issue is already covered under the theming roadmap (#236), and the lint test failure is a known issue on main that I'll mention in the summary rather than file separately since it's lower priority.

For the issue bodies, I'll include what's wrong, why it matters, the suggested fix, and evidence to back each one up. I'll stick with just the "see-something" label to avoid label creation errors.
I found three new issues to file: two capture bugs and a wordTimings persistence gap, all confirmed as distinct from existing issues. Now I'll file them per the see-something policy.

unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue create --title "[see-something] correctness: system tap ignores mid-session sample-rate changes — WAV timeline stretched ~1.6-1.9x, breaks diarization + transcript timestamps (CoreAudioTapCaptureActorSupport.swift:144)" --label "see-something" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What's wrong

`CoreAudioTapCaptureActor` captures `inputFormat = newEngine.inputNode.inputFormat(forBus: 0)` once during `setupAggregateAndEngine` (CoreAudioTapCaptureActorSupport.swift:144) and derives the AVAudioConverter ratio from it (`ratio = configuration.sampleRate / inputFormat.sampleRate`). There is **no `AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` observer on this engine** — unlike `MicCaptureActor`, which got exactly this handling in #49 (`MicCaptureActorRouteChange.swift`).

When the tapped output device changes sample rate mid-session (e.g. Bluetooth headset renegotiating A2DP↔HFP when the mic engages — which THE RECORD itself triggers via `MicCaptureActor`), the tap keeps delivering buffers at the new rate while the converter still assumes the old one. The output WAV then contains time-stretched audio.

## Evidence (production data, ~/Library/Application Support/THE RECORD)

Recording `F7C8DEAE-18DF-4853-B0D0-313FB81860BC` (2026-06-22):
- File birth→mtime: 14:25:03 → 14:25:34 = **31 s wall time** (DB duration 31.195 s, mic-cleaned file 29.856 s — both agree)
- Main WAV `2026-06-22T20:25:03Z.wav`: **57.685 s** @16 kHz (922,960 frames) — **1.85× wall time**
- Signal analysis: zero duplicated blocks, no long-lag self-similarity (probe correlation matches only itself), pitch **bimodal** (~99 Hz and ~186 Hz clusters) → part of the session is rate-stretched, part normal → rate changed mid-session
- Second recording `F34D479A` (2026-06-18): WAV 10.085 s vs 6.23 s wall = **1.62×** — ratio varies with when the change occurred

## Why it matters

This corrupts the single source of truth for the whole pipeline:
- Batch transcription (StopAndTranscribeUseCase) transcribes stretched audio → degraded text + timestamps on a fake 0–57.7 s timeline
- Diarization (DiarizeMeetingUseCase) runs on the same file → speaker boundaries align to noise; observed segments alternate "1"/"Unknown" across 0–57.68 s for a 31 s session. **This is the root cause of "diarization doesn't work".**
- `audioDuration = samples/16000` disagrees with DB wall-time duration

## Suggested fix

Mirror the #49 fix on the system-tap engine:
1. Observe `.AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` for the tap engine; on fire, re-read `inputNode.inputFormat(forBus: 0)` and rebuild the `AVAudioConverter` (and tap) with the new input format.
2. Defensively, compare `inBuffer.format.sampleRate` against the assumed `inputFormat.sampleRate` inside the tap callback and rebuild the converter on mismatch — the buffer's own format is authoritative.
3. Log the change (relates to #194 — converter errors in this callback are currently silent).

Related: #49 (same bug fixed for MicCaptureActor), #194 (silent converter errors in the same callback).
EOF
)"

# Issue drafts — 2026-07-01 session (blocked from filing; run manually if approved)

## Draft 1 — THE diarization root cause

```bash
unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue create \
  --title "[see-something] correctness: system tap ignores mid-session sample-rate changes — WAV timeline stretched ~1.6-1.9x, breaks diarization + transcript timestamps (CoreAudioTapCaptureActorSupport.swift:144)" \
  --label "see-something" \
  --body-file .temp/issue-body-tap-rate.md
```

### Body (`.temp/issue-body-tap-rate.md`)

**What's wrong.** `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor` captures `inputFormat = newEngine.inputNode.inputFormat(forBus: 0)` once during `setupAggregateAndEngine` (CoreAudioTapCaptureActorSupport.swift:144) and derives the AVAudioConverter ratio from it (`ratio = configuration.sampleRate / inputFormat.sampleRate`). There is **no `AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` observer on this engine** — unlike `MicCaptureActor`, which got exactly this handling in #49 (`MicCaptureActorRouteChange.swift`). When the tapped output device changes sample rate mid-session (e.g. Bluetooth headset renegotiating A2DP↔HFP when the mic engages — which THE RECORD itself triggers via `MicCaptureActor`), the tap keeps delivering buffers at the new rate while the converter still assumes the old one → time-stretched WAV.

**Evidence (production data, ~/Library/Application Support/THE RECORD).** Recording `F7C8DEAE-18DF-4853-B0D0-313FB81860BC` (2026-06-22): file birth→mtime 14:25:03→14:25:34 = **31 s wall time** (DB duration 31.195 s, mic-cleaned file 29.856 s — both agree), but main WAV `2026-06-22T20:25:03Z.wav` holds **57.685 s** @16 kHz (922,960 frames) = **1.85× wall time**. Signal analysis: zero duplicated blocks, no long-lag self-similarity (a 1 s probe matches only itself), pitch **bimodal** (~99 Hz and ~186 Hz clusters) → part of the session is rate-stretched, part normal → the rate changed mid-session. Second recording `F34D479A` (2026-06-18): WAV 10.085 s vs 6.23 s wall = **1.62×** — ratio varies with when the change occurred.

**Why it matters.** The main WAV is the single source of truth for the pipeline: batch transcription produces degraded text with timestamps on a fake 0–57.7 s timeline; diarization aligns speaker boundaries to that same corrupted audio (observed segments alternate "1"/"Unknown" across 0–57.68 s for a 31 s session). **This is the root cause of "diarization doesn't work."**

**Suggested fix.** Mirror the #49 fix on the system-tap engine: (1) observe `.AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange`, re-read `inputNode.inputFormat(forBus: 0)`, rebuild the converter+tap; (2) defensively compare `inBuffer.format.sampleRate` against the assumed rate inside the tap callback and rebuild on mismatch — the buffer's own format is authoritative; (3) log the change (relates to #194 — converter errors in this callback are currently silent).

Related: #49 (same bug fixed for MicCaptureActor), #194.

## Draft 2 — silent mic-cleaned WAV

```bash
unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue create \
  --title "[see-something] correctness: mic-cleaned WAV is pure digital silence in production — AEC/sink chain writes no signal (AECProcessorActor.swift, WAVCleanedAudioSink)" \
  --label "see-something" \
  --body-file .temp/issue-body-silent-mic.md
```

### Body (`.temp/issue-body-silent-mic.md`)

**What's wrong.** Both production `-mic-cleaned.wav` files (2026-06-18, 2026-06-22) contain **no signal at all**: average spectrum is −180 dB across every band 0–8 kHz. The file has the right duration (≈ wall time) but every sample is zero. So the mic → AEC → `CleanedAudioSink` chain runs, paces correctly, and writes silence.

**Why it matters.** The cleaned-mic track exists to feed the cleanup re-transcription pass (`cleaned_mic_audio_url`, `needs_retranscription`); a silent file means that pass transcribes nothing and the user's own voice is lost from the archive. Likely interacts with #190 (AEC truncates every mic buffer to 256 samples) and #192 (WAVWriter errorHandler never wired — failures invisible).

**Suggested fix.** Instrument the AEC output path with an RMS check (log if N consecutive cleaned buffers are all-zero); verify SpeexDSP echo-cancellation state isn't cancelling the entire near-end signal (e.g. mic signal fed as both near and far end); add an integration test asserting non-zero RMS through `AECProcessorActor` for a synthetic voice buffer.

Related: #190, #192, #231 (WAVCleanedAudioSink coupling).

## Draft 3 — stale word_timings on re-diarization

```bash
unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue create \
  --title "[see-something] silent-bug: attachDiarization upsert never clears word_timings — stale timings survive re-diarization (GRDBStorageActor+Diarization.swift:40)" \
  --label "see-something" \
  --body-file .temp/issue-body-word-timings.md
```

### Body (`.temp/issue-body-word-timings.md`)

**What's wrong.** `attachDiarization` upserts segments via `GRDBSQL.upsertSegment`, whose `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` sets text/speaker/start/end/confidence but **not `word_timings`** — and `DiarizedSegment.wordTimings` from the incoming transcript is never written. `getSegments` reads `word_timings` back and attaches it to whatever text now occupies that `segment_index`.

**Why it matters.** After any re-diarization (repair pipeline, cleanup pass), segment N's text/boundaries change but its old `word_timings` JSON remains → word-level highlighting/alignment silently points at the wrong words.

**Suggested fix.** Either persist `seg.wordTimings` in the upsert (add the column to `upsertSegment` with excluded update), or explicitly `SET word_timings = NULL` on conflict so stale data can't survive.

With the embedding path in play, this could easily match.

The first test "embeddingAvailable" passed and expects embeddings to be available, so they're definitely loaded on this machine. The old code took the same embedding path with the same `embeddingVector(for:)` call, so the behavior should be identical—this looks like a pre-existing issue where the threshold is simply too low for embedding-based matching. It might pass on CI if embeddings aren't available there, forcing the fuzzy path where string similarity between unrelated queries stays below 0.1, but on my machine with embeddings loaded, it fails. The real problem is that 0.1 is far too permissive for cosine similarity thresholds.

For the caching test, the provider seems to be finding a semantic match for the second query even though it's different, so it's returning a cached result instead of calling the inner provider. If CachingContextProvider uses semantic matching with a low threshold, different queries can incorrectly match. The raw audio changes stream uses a buffer that keeps the latest 64 events, so even if a listener connects late, they'll still receive the buffered state changes.

The real problem emerges from the timing of `refreshCalendar`: it clears `armedMeeting` first, then calls `calendar.upcomingMeetings` to find the next meeting and schedule an arm. With a meeting 3 minutes away and a 600-second arm window, the delay calculates to negative, so it arms immediately — normally within 100ms. But under concurrent test load with multiple suites running in parallel, that 100ms sleep can elapse before the entire chain completes (init task → start → refresh task → await upcoming meetings → schedule arm task → sleep → actual arm). The fix isn't a longer sleep — it's polling until the meeting is actually armed instead of relying on a fixed delay, but the detector doesn't expose its armed state publicly for tests to observe.
